title.en: Mehar and the Moon in the Lake
title.de: Mehar und der Mond im See

inspired_by: The Elephants and the Hares, from the Panchatantra
learning: Cleverness beats size, and big ones should watch out for small ones

characters.name: Gajraj
characters.who: the big elephant king, thirsty and in a hurry

characters.name: Hasi
characters.who: a small bunny with long ears and a brave heart

characters.name: Chanda Mama
characters.who: the moon, who shines on the lake

pages.text: The Panchatantra book glowed. Whoosh! Mehar landed in a dry, dusty jungle. No rain had fallen for months. The grass was brown, and the elephants were very, very thirsty.
Gajraj, the elephant king, found a sparkling lake. "Water!" he trumpeted. The whole herd ran. STOMP! STOMP! STOMP! Right over the little bunny burrows on the shore.
Hasi the bunny sat by her squashed home. "They will come back every night," she sniffed. "What can tiny bunnies do against big elephants?" Mehar hugged her tight.
Mehar looked up at the round full moon. Then she looked down at the lake. There was the moon again, floating in the water! "Hasi, I have an idea!" Can you guess it?
Next night, Hasi hopped onto a tall rock. "Stop, King Gajraj! I bring a message from the Moon. This is the Moon's own lake, and you squashed the Moon's bunnies!"
Gajraj laughed. "The Moon? Where?" "Look in the lake," said Mehar. Gajraj peeked. There she was, round and shining in the water! "Oh!" he gulped.
"Sorry, Moon!" Gajraj dipped his trunk to say hello... SPLISH! The water rippled, and the moon wobbled and shook into pieces. "She's shaking! She's cross with me!"
Gajraj's big knees trembled. "What shall I do?" Mehar stepped forward. "Walk softly. Go around the burrows, and drink only from the far side of the lake."
Tiptoe, tiptoe! The whole herd walked carefully around the bunny homes. Gajraj even helped Hasi pat her burrow back into shape with his trunk.
Then Hasi giggled and told him the truth. "The moon in the lake is only a reflection!" Gajraj blinked. Then he laughed. "Clever little ones! You taught me to watch my step."
Whoosh! Mehar was back in bed. In her glass of water by the window, a tiny moon was shining. "Good night, Moon," she whispered. "Good night, Hasi."

moral.en: Being clever is stronger than being big. And the biggest ones should always watch where they step, and look out for the small.
moral.de: Klugheit ist stärker als Größe. Und die Großen sollen auf die Kleinen achten.
moral.hi: चतुराई ताक़त से बड़ी होती है। और बड़ों को छोटों का ध्यान रखना चाहिए।
moral.hi_roman: Chaturaai taakat se badi hoti hai. Aur badon ko chhoton ka dhyaan rakhna chahiye.

questions.en: What did Gajraj see when he looked into the lake?
Have you ever seen the moon in water? Where?
